description: Review-oriented 12-sample benchmark pack for dossier_v1 iteration. Keeps the stratified_v1 source pool but reorders it into meaningful balanced prefixes.
selection_rationale: Keep the proven 12 source items from stratified_v1_12sample, but attach explicit review axes and reorder them so quick prefix runs do not silently collapse to single-point-only coverage.
ordering_rationale: The first 4 items cover four goal families across both single-point and multi-point aux. The first 6 items cover all six core goal families with a 3 single-point / 3 multi-point split.
acceptance_policy: No numeric threshold in this manifest implies data-quality acceptance. Surface metrics and review tallies still require semantic review against docs/immutable/DATA_QUALITY_REQUIREMENTS.md.

review_axis_definitions.visible_only_boundary: Check that the final thinking reads as image-and-problem-only reasoning and does not slip into hidden-proof phrasing or internal schema references.
review_axis_definitions.whole_figure_coverage: Check that the route uses non-anchor visible structure and does not stay trapped around the first 2-3 named points.
review_axis_definitions.coordinate_integration: Check that coordinate or visual cues enter the actual reasoning chain rather than appearing as decorative labels.
review_axis_definitions.aux_to_goal_closure: Check that the text really closes the chain from aux immediate effects through bridge steps to the goal-side finish.
review_axis_definitions.single_point_necessity: Check that the single helper point is motivated as a necessary bridge and not as an arbitrary add-on.
review_axis_definitions.multi_point_staging: Check that each auxiliary point has an explicit staged role and the route does not flatten the construction into one lump.

record_annotation_guide.route_depth_hint: A rough hint for how long and failure-prone the back-half closure tends to be. It is a review-priority hint, not an automatic metric.
record_annotation_guide.figure_span_hint: A rough hint for how broad the visible structure is that should enter the reasoning. It helps target full-figure coverage review.
record_annotation_guide.coordinate_dependency_hint: A rough hint for how much the sample relies on coordinate or image-derived cues to stay credible.
record_annotation_guide.must_check: The highest-priority review axes that should be checked first on this sample.
record_annotation_guide.review_prompts: Concrete human-review prompts that tie the sample back to the immutable data-quality requirements.

records.goal_text: eqratio a e b d e g b f
review_prompts: Does the midpoint-style cue actually enter the ratio chain, or is it only mentioned near the start?
After the helper point is added, does the text explicitly close the ratio route instead of stopping at a plausible local balance?
records.notes: Single midpoint-style helper. Useful for checking whether one local balance cue actually closes a ratio chain.

records.goal_text: eqangle a e c e d f c f
review_prompts: Is the multi-point construction explained as a real sequence of steps, with each point unlocking a distinct relation?
Does the angle route reconnect to the broader visible figure, or does it stay inside the helper frame too long?
records.notes: Balanced-prefix multi-point angle case. Useful for checking staged collinear plus perpendicular narration.

records.goal_text: simtri a c g f a g
review_prompts: Does the text keep the cyclic route visible-only, or does it drift into proof-engine style circle talk?
Is the single helper point justified as necessary before the similarity closure is claimed?
records.notes: Single-point double-cyclic case. Useful for checking whether circle talk stays grounded and still closes to similarity.

records.goal_text: simtrir a g i i g h
review_prompts: Do the parallel and perpendicular cues genuinely drive the reverse-similarity route, or are they just named and abandoned?
Is the final reverse-similarity closure explicit, or does the route jump over the last bridge?
records.notes: Balanced-prefix reverse-similarity case. Useful for checking whether mixed helper mechanisms stay explicit and ordered.

records.goal_text: contri b c f f e b
review_prompts: Does the right-angle or perpendicular support actually justify the congruence route?
Is the single helper point shown to be the needed bridge into the congruence closure?
records.notes: Single-point congruence case. Useful for checking whether the helper is necessary and the triangle closure is real.

records.goal_text: contrir a c h d b h
review_prompts: Does the midpoint language stay concrete and get reused later, or does it dissolve into vague helper narration?
Does the reasoning use enough of the visible frame beyond the new points to make the reverse-congruence finish credible?
records.notes: Balanced-prefix reverse-congruence case. Useful for checking staged midpoint language in a larger visible frame.

records.goal_text: eqangle a b a c a d a e
review_prompts: Does the angle closure remain grounded in visible cyclic and collinear facts rather than proof shorthand?
Even though the helper is only one point, does the reasoning still use enough of the whole figure?
records.notes: Single-point cyclic plus collinear angle case. Useful for checking whether angle closure stays visible-only and non-tautological.

records.goal_text: eqratio b e c e d e b e
review_prompts: Does the text keep the roles of the multiple helper mechanisms separate before they are merged into the ratio chain?
Is the final ratio closure explicit and complete, rather than implied by a generic similarity claim?
records.notes: Multi-point ratio case. Useful for checking whether several helper mechanisms still close one clean ratio chain.

records.goal_text: simtrir b d e c e g
review_prompts: Do the parallel and perpendicular cues enter the first real bridge, or are they only used as scene-setting?
Does the final similarity route reuse those cues explicitly enough to justify the reverse-similarity finish?
records.notes: Single-point reverse-similarity case. Useful for checking whether parallel and perpendicular cues truly support the similarity route.

records.goal_text: contri a b d c d b
review_prompts: Does the route explain why each added point exists before claiming the congruence finish?
Does the text keep using the old visible frame, or does it collapse into helper-only narration?
records.notes: Multi-point congruence case. Useful for checking whether a longer staged helper route stays explicit instead of collapsing into shorthand.

records.goal_text: contrir b d i i f b
review_prompts: Is the angle-transfer story actually supported by visible relations, or does it smuggle in hidden-route confidence?
Do the coordinate or perpendicular cues stay alive through the final reverse-congruence closure?
records.notes: Single-point reverse-congruence case. Useful for checking whether angle transfer language is actually supported.

records.goal_text: simtri a b e d c a
review_prompts: Does the route stay figure-grounded after the helper expands, or does it drift into abstract cyclic shorthand?
When the text claims the similarity finish, are the last 2-4 steps really present and justified?
records.notes: Multi-point similarity case. Useful for checking whether the route stays figure-grounded after several helper steps.
